summary_1line: Narada recounts Pulastya’s teaching to Bhishma on the virtues of pilgrimage and describes the immense spiritual merit of visiting Pushkara and many other sacred tirthas.

image_candidates.scene_text: The austere Bhishma, emaciated from vows, stands with joined hands offering arghya as the radiant sage Pulastya appears before him near the source of the Ganga.
At Pushkara’s sacred lake during twilight, countless gods, rishis, and celestial beings gather invisibly around pilgrims bathing in the holy waters.
A lone pilgrim walks the long path between remote tirthas—rivers, forests, and shrines—seeking merit greater than grand sacrifices.
